high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless De’VIA screenprint: four Deaf collaborators use an equal flat layout, raised relief, modular pieces and signed conversation to change one central branching construction; every form is a bold red, cobalt, black or cream silhouette with centralized hands and eyes, no gradients, realistic depth, writing or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A flat cream field fills the page around one central black disk, with four equal cobalt and red corner masses pulling attention back toward the middle. Every shape occupies one frontal plane with hard boundaries and high contrast. No architectural studio, wall, window, realistic floor, perspective recession, written language, alphabet, caption, numeral, arrow, diagram connector, medical chart, hearing test, broken ear, cochlear device, charity symbol, ranking badge, stage, podium, clinical furniture, or national flag appears.

elements.desc: Large shared circular worktable at the center, matte black with a cream rim and clear space around every participant. A low articulated mobile rises from its middle: one cobalt trunk divides into three red branches ending in a cream circle, black crescent, and cobalt square, with every joint reachable by hand and no screen, label, button text, or privileged side.

Adult Deaf visual artist seated at the upper-left side, light-brown skin, close-cropped black curls, red long-sleeve shirt, charcoal trousers, and black shoes. With an attentive direct gaze, they rearrange the cream circle on a high-contrast flat layout matching the central mobile exactly, while their free hand remains visible and no medical device or authority marker appears.

Adult Deaf tactile artist seated at the upper-right side at equal scale, dark-brown skin, long black braids, cobalt blouse, cream trousers, and dark shoes. Both hands explore an equivalent raised relief of the same trunk, three branches, circle, crescent, and square; one red branch piece can be repositioned, making this surface an active construction rather than a passive description.

Adult Deaf participant seated at the lower-left side, medium-brown skin, straight dark hair at jaw length, cream jacket, black shirt, cobalt trousers, and red shoes. They hold the matching cobalt square modular piece beside the central mobile’s open lower joint, ready to enact the shared change; their posture is relaxed, capable, and free of helper, patient, or spectator framing.

Adult Deaf facilitator seated at the lower-right side, medium-brown skin, short wavy gray hair, black shirt, red vest, cream trousers, and cobalt shoes. They use clear natural signed conversation toward the group, with both anatomically complete hands separated against the cream field; no claim is made that a specific lexical sign is reproduced, and no one awaits permission from them.

High-contrast flat layout resting before the first artist, a cream rectangle carrying the exact cobalt trunk, three red branches, cream circle, black crescent, and cobalt square of the central mobile in the same spatial order. Every shape is detachable and equal in size to its modular counterpart; the surface contains no text, border legend, arrow, key, or status color.

Raised tactile relief resting before the second artist, a black rectangle carrying the exact same trunk, branch lengths, junctions, circle, crescent, and square as the flat layout and central mobile. Thick cream outlines and distinct surface textures make every part touch-readable and movable; it has no Braille text, caption, audio icon, clinical marking, or simplified missing branch.
